literal: At all the places where obstructed, like a bull, he who is; the distress encountered by him will suffer distress.
translation: Like a strong bull that pulls a cart through every obstacle, he who perseveres will cause distress itself to suffer distress.
modern: தடைகள் ஏற்படும் இடங்களிலெல்லாம் வண்டியை இழுத்துச் செல்லும் எருதைப் போன்ற விடாமுயற்சி உடையவன் அடையும் துன்பமானது, அத்துன்பத்திற்கே துன்பத்தை உண்டாக்கிவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful agricultural metaphor to describe resilience. A strong draft bull (பகடு) does not stop when its cart gets stuck in mud or encounters obstacles (மடுத்த வாய் எல்லாம்); it exerts more strength and pulls through. A person who faces life's obstacles with the same relentless determination will find that the distress (இடுக்கண்) they encounter is itself defeated and made to suffer (இடர்ப்பாடு உடைத்து). Through this image, the poet shows that active perseverance turns the tables on adversity.
